verdict: This is not the marginal PF 1.10 / +0.068R engine the fact pack's headline describes, and four of the five analysts built their case on that headline. The replay scores every signal generateSignal emits, including 354 closed trades below the live confidenceThreshold of 70 that the live system would never open; those 354 trades carry -49.26R. Condition on what the live gate actually admits (conf>=70) and the same replay is 303 closed, PF 1.48, +93.96R, expectancyR +0.310. Nearly every 'loss pattern' in the reports dissolves under that one condition plus the removal of one asset: the adx20-30 'dead zone' becomes +19.47R / PF 1.28; MIXED trend shrinks from -21.38R to -2.09R; SELL direction goes to PF 1.00 / -0.08R; rsi<35 ex-SPX goes to -2.80R over 78 closed; DAILY+H4_CONFLICT disappears entirely (its highest conf is 45); and the MODERATE-vs-STRONG gap vanishes (0.309 vs 0.319) because STRONG is simply a conf>=95 label, not an independent quality tier. What is actually wrong is narrower and worse than any single report says. First, SPX MOMENTUM is 3 wins in 55 closed (PF 0.11, -48.59R; 26 closed and -20.83R even above the confidence gate) while the identical setup wins 49.1% on BTC/Gold above the gate (165 closed, PF 2.32, +116.42R), and 63 of SPX's 130 trades never resolve at all (48% expiry vs 12.6% BTC / 18.9% Gold). A setup cannot lose that specifically on one instrument for strategy reasons: that is a per-instrument level/stop-target scaling or symbol-mapping defect, and it alone drags a +115.84R book down to +93.96R. Second, none of this is live-validated: 11 journal entries, 9 recorded learning outcomes across 218 sessions, a MOMENTUM learning record showing 3W/1L with negative PnL, an AI filter that has never evaluated a single trade, and a healer reporting ok:true on every one of those. The strategy edge is fine and largely already gated; the measurement, learning and execution plumbing is what is broken, and the biggest real risk right now is that the system auto-tunes or filters itself on this pack's confounded aggregates and destroys a working edge.

actions.action: Stop opening SPX positions immediately (add a per-asset kill switch / disabledAssets = ["SPX"]), and open a defect investigation into SPX stop and target level scaling rather than treating SPX as a strategy that needs filtering.
actions.rationale: SPX is 67 closed, 6 wins (9.0%), PF 0.19, -51.64R against a whole-book +44.7R. It survives every confound: above the live conf>=70 gate SPX is still 27 closed, 7.4% WR, PF 0.17, -21.88R, and removing it lifts the live-admissible book from +93.96R / PF 1.48 / 0.310R to +115.84R / PF 1.69 / 0.420R. The failure is concentrated entirely in MOMENTUM (55 closed, 3 wins, PF 0.11, -48.59R), the same setup that wins 49.1% at PF 2.32 on BTC and Gold above the gate, and 48% of SPX trades (63 of 130) expire without resolving versus 12.6% on BTC and 18.9% on Gold. No indicator explains it: SPX bandwidth 5.81 is close to Gold's 6.01 (the best asset), adx mean 22.7, rr almost always 2.0. A setup that wins 40-49% on two instruments and 5.5% on a third, with half its trades unable to reach either level, is mis-scaled levels or a bad symbol/feed mapping, not a lost edge.
actions.measurableWhy: The replay runs generateSignal per asset, so excluding SPX is a direct re-run and the -51.64R / -21.88R deltas recompute exactly. The replay can also confirm the bug hypothesis by comparing generated stop/target distances against realised SPX bar ranges, which is where the 48% expiry rate should show up.
actions.agreement: loss-autopsy and risk-and-config both propose it and are the only two analysts who examined the asset dimension at all; setup-forensics, strength-gate and regime-fit never look at byAsset and therefore misattribute SPX's damage to setups, regimes and strength tiers.
actions.risk: 63 of 130 SPX trades are still open, so the closed sample is resolution-biased toward trades that already hit a level; a 9.0% win rate sits far outside that bias, but the true -51.64R may soften. Removes all index exposure and concentrates the book into one crypto and one metal. Disabling also hides the underlying defect, so the kill switch must be paired with the investigation, not substituted for it.

actions.action: Do not raise adxTrendingMin. Pin it at 20 and remove it from autoTunableSettings until there is a measured reason to move it.
actions.rationale: Two analysts recommend raising it to 25-30 on the grounds that adx20-30 is the only negative ADX band (244 closed, PF 0.94, -10.03R). That negativity is entirely SPX plus sub-threshold flow. Ex-SPX, adx20-30 is +5.63R / PF 1.04; above the live conf>=70 gate it is +19.47R / PF 1.28 / expectancyR +0.179 - profitable. Raising the threshold would push profitable flow out of TRENDING and shrink the regime that holds MOMENTUM's largest and best block (139 closed at conf>=70 ex-SPX, 46.8% WR, PF 2.23, +95.72R). Because adxTrendingMin is the system's only auto-tunable knob, an auto-tuner fed this pack's aggregates will make exactly this move. Preventing a roughly -19R regression at zero cost is the second-highest expected value available, and it costs nothing to hold.
actions.suggestedValues: 20 (hold; do not sweep on this fact pack)
actions.measurableWhy: adxTrendingMin is explicitly visible to the replay and is the one parameter it can sweep end to end. A sweep at 20/25/30 restricted to conf>=70 and excluding SPX will confirm that raising it removes positive-expectancy flow - run that before letting any tuner touch it.
actions.agreement: loss-autopsy alone (proposal to freeze adxTrendingMin, on the grounds that ADX win rates are flat at 33.2/32.8/34.2%). regime-fit and risk-and-config both propose raising it and the FACTS contradict them - see disagreements. setup-forensics proposes only a diagnostic sweep, which is compatible with holding.
actions.risk: Removes the system's only automatic adaptation path. If genuine ADX sensitivity emerges on a larger, SPX-free, above-threshold sample, a pinned threshold will not track it - so this is a hold pending better data, not a permanent freeze.

actions.action: Disable BUY_OVERSOLD entirely - stop generating and executing it, do not downweight it.
actions.rationale: It is the only losing setup whose loss survives both confounds cleanly. Overall 15 closed, 3 wins (20.0%), PF 0.45, -6.96R, expectancyR -0.464 - the worst non-noise bucket in the pack. Above the live conf>=70 gate it is 6 closed, 0 wins, -6.30R at -1.05R each, i.e. every high-confidence BUY_OVERSOLD trade was a full stop. Its RANGING leg is 0 wins in 7 closed. No sub-bucket above minSample rescues it, so there is no gate to write - only removal. It is also the true content of two separate 'findings' elsewhere in the reports: it is the whole of the rsi<35 BUY loss and a third of the MIXED-trend loss ex-SPX, so killing the setup collects those without adding blunt indicator filters.
actions.measurableWhy: Setup selection is generateSignal logic, which is exactly what the replay executes; removing the setup and re-running recomputes the -6.96R delta directly.
actions.agreement: setup-forensics (disable outright) and strength-gate (first setup to lose MODERATE eligibility) agree directly; regime-fit and risk-and-config target it indirectly via a minEntryRsi floor, which is the wrong instrument for the same problem - see disagreements.
actions.risk: Only 15 closed and 6 above the gate, so the true edge could be less negative than -0.464R. If BUY_OVERSOLD is the primary long mean-reversion entry, the book becomes even more concentrated in MOMENTUM, which already carries essentially all the profit.

actions.action: Gate SQUEEZE_BREAKOUT to the RANGING regime only - block it in TRENDING and SQUEEZE - implemented as a per-setup allowed-regime map at signal generation so the same mechanism can carry future regime rules.
actions.rationale: This is the largest negative setup by volume that survives the live confidence gate: 84 closed at conf>=70, PF 0.93, -4.20R. Ex-SPX and above the gate the legs separate cleanly: TRENDING 43 closed, PF 0.90, -3.15R; SQUEEZE 20 closed, PF 0.78, -3.50R; RANGING 20 closed, PF 1.26, +3.50R. The setup loses in its own namesake regime and only works in the opposite one, which is a genuine inversion rather than a sample artefact - it holds on the full sample, ex-SPX, and above the gate. Per-trade impact is modest (-0.05R) but it is the only remaining structural leak with real volume behind it, and building the regime-map mechanism here pays for itself later.
actions.measurableWhy: Both the setup and the regime label are computed inside generateSignal, so the replay can apply the gate and re-measure. Measure the result restricted to conf>=70 and excluding SPX, or the confounds will swamp the effect.
actions.agreement: setup-forensics and regime-fit propose the identical gate independently; strength-gate proposes keeping it as data-collection-only, which is a weaker version of the same judgement (it agrees the bucket is a drag, and at PF 0.92-0.93 it is close enough to breakeven that the data argument has some force).
actions.risk: The retained RANGING leg is only 20 closed trades, so the surviving edge is not firmly established and the setup could still be a net drag. If the regime classifier is noisy near its boundary the gate may relabel rather than remove the losing trades - which is another reason not to move adxTrendingMin underneath it (see rank 2).

actions.action: Repair the outcome-recording plumbing: write every closed trade to the journal and learning store, reconcile setup names against the nine traded setups, fix the PnL sign error, and change the healer's learningFile, journalFile and aiFilter checks to fail when they are empty or far below the trade count instead of passing on any non-zero value.
actions.rationale: No R effect and no R risk, which makes it the best profitability-per-unit-of-risk item that is not a trade decision. Right now the learning store holds 9 outcomes across 4 setups over 218 sessions against 9 traded setups; one of those 4 (BB_SQUEEZE_WATCH) never appears in the traded book; MOMENTUM is recorded 3W/1L with totalPnl -32.03, which cannot be reconciled with PF 1.25 / +67.39R; the journal holds 11 entries; and the AI filter has evaluated zero trades. Every one of these reports ok:true and healer.healthy is true with healCount 0. That means the system currently cannot validate any action on this list, and it is calibrating on 9 data points while reporting itself healthy. Fixing this is the precondition for trusting anything ranked above or below it.
actions.measurableWhy: This is live telemetry and healer logic, not signal generation. The replay never touches the journal, the learning store or the AI filter, and cannot exercise a health check. Verification has to come from live runs after the fix.
actions.agreement: strength-gate (investigate why the learner has 9 outcomes against 657 closed) and risk-and-config (repair the learning pipeline, make aiFilter fail when unexercised, make journalFile fail on the 11-vs-826 gap) converge on this from opposite directions; loss-autopsy independently notes the aiFilter is inert.
actions.risk: Once the AI filter actually runs it will start rejecting trades on logic never exercised against any of the 826 trades, so live behaviour could shift sharply in either direction - stage it behind a log-only mode first. Repopulating the learning file will also discontinuously shift any calibration currently derived from it. If the 11 journal entries are legitimately a different record type from replay trades, a naive count-comparison check will alarm permanently and desensitise the healer.

actions.action: Determine from the code whether dailyOnlyMinConfidence = 0 lets daily-only signals bypass the global confidenceThreshold of 70. If it does, set it to 70 to close the hole; if it does not, leave it at 0 and take no action.
actions.rationale: Two analysts want this raised to 70-80 on the strength of DAILY_ONLY_H4_NEUTRAL's 18.5% win rate, and they are wrong about the cohort - above the gate it is the best cohort in the book (27 closed, PF 2.49, +32.75R, expectancyR +1.213) and 87% of its sub-threshold damage is SPX (-32.10R of -37.09R; ex-SPX only -4.99R over 60 closed). But the underlying question is real and unanswered by the facts: a setting named dailyOnlyMinConfidence sitting at 0 alongside a global threshold of 70 is ambiguous, and if it is a separate lower floor for that cohort then daily-only signals are entering live below 70 and the -4.99R ex-SPX sub-threshold flow is being traded. Cheap to check, bounded upside, and it prevents the aggressive 70-80 setting two analysts recommend from cutting a +1.213R cohort.
actions.suggestedValues: 70 only if a bypass exists; otherwise leave at 0. Do not use 75 or 80.
actions.measurableWhy: The replay cannot see confidenceThreshold at all, and the cohort label depends on multi-timeframe agreement computed in generateSignalMTF, which the replay also cannot exercise - the cohort field in the fact pack is reconstructed post hoc, not produced by the live combiner. Both halves of this action are invisible to the replay; it must be resolved by reading the code and then confirmed live.
actions.agreement: loss-autopsy and risk-and-config both propose raising it, but for a reason the FACTS refute; risk-and-config separately and correctly flags that the setting is switched off. The action is kept, the rationale is replaced, and their suggested values are rejected.
actions.risk: Setting it to 70 when no bypass exists is a harmless no-op; setting it to 75 or 80 as proposed would cut into the cohort's above-gate flow, which is the highest-expectancy cohort measured. The cohort's 27 above-gate closed trades are a thin basis for that +1.213R figure, so do not over-read it in either direction.

gate.detail: dailyOnlyMinConfidence is outside what the replay can see (adxTrendingMin) — needs a human decision

actions.action: Move sizing off fixed lots: set fixedLotSize to 0 and set riskPercent explicitly (start at 0.5), staged and monitored, so every trade risks the same fraction of equity.
actions.rationale: fixedLotSize is 0.02 and riskPercent is absent from active settings entirely - it exists only in the limits block. A constant lot across BTC, Gold and SPX is a very different money risk per trade, which means the R unit underpinning every finding in this pack is not constant and cross-asset comparisons are not strictly valid. This matters most for the rank-1 decision: SPX's -51.64R and Gold's +69.42R are not necessarily comparable dollar magnitudes. Directly relevant to profitability per unit of risk, which is the ranking criterion, but it is a live-sizing change with real downside so it sits below the changes that only remove flow.
actions.measurableWhy: Position sizing is enforced by the MT5 bridge, not by generateSignal. The replay is denominated in R and is sizing-agnostic by construction, so it cannot show any effect from this change.
actions.agreement: risk-and-config only; no other analyst examined sizing. The point stands on its own because it is a direct reading of liveState.strategySettings rather than an inference from a bucket.
actions.risk: Live position sizes change immediately and could be materially larger than 0.02 lots on some instruments, with maxLotSize 10 as the only backstop - this must be staged and watched. It also breaks comparability with the existing 826-trade history, so do it after the rank-1 through rank-4 measurements are taken, not before.

gate.detail: fixedLotSize is outside what the replay can see (adxTrendingMin) — needs a human decision

actions.action: Gate RANGE_TRADE_SHORT to TRENDING only (block RANGING and SQUEEZE) - but treat it as housekeeping, not as a profitability lever, and do not spend implementation priority on it ahead of ranks 1-5.
actions.rationale: Three analysts make this their headline finding and the regime inversion is real on the full sample: TRENDING 27 closed, PF 1.30, +4.71R against RANGING 22 closed, PF 0.42, -11.05R and SQUEEZE 9 closed, PF 0.41, -4.30R. But almost none of it is live flow. Above the conf>=70 gate the entire setup is 10 closed trades worth +0.17R, split TRENDING 6 closed (+1.75R) and SQUEEZE 4 closed (-1.58R) - the -10.19R the analysts are chasing is 50 sub-threshold trades the live system never opens. The gate is still the right shape and costs nothing once the regime-map from rank 4 exists, so ship it with that mechanism; just do not expect live P&L from it. It also absorbs most of the 'shorts lose' and 'MIXED trend loses' findings, which are the same 60 trades relabelled.
actions.measurableWhy: Setup and regime are both generateSignal outputs, so the replay measures this directly - but it must be measured restricted to conf>=70, or the replay will report a large improvement that cannot occur live.
actions.agreement: setup-forensics, regime-fit and risk-and-config all propose it (risk-and-config via a per-setup STRONG requirement, which for this setup is equivalent to a disable). Unanimity among the three is why it is on the list at all; the confidence-conditioned data is why it is rank 8 rather than rank 1.
actions.risk: Cuts the setup to roughly 27 closed trades of historical support and only 6 above the gate, so the retained edge is very sample-fragile and sits in the setup's non-design regime - a classic slice-until-positive result. Disabling the setup outright is the more honest alternative and costs only the +4.71R TRENDING cell.

actions.action: Do not increase position size on MOMENTUM|SQUEEZE or MOMENTUM|STRONG yet. Instrument these cells and revisit once each has 40+ closed trades above the confidence gate.
actions.rationale: MOMENTUM|SQUEEZE is genuinely the best pocket measured - 43 closed, 53.5% WR, PF 2.14, +0.555R, and 18 closed at 66.7% / PF 3.71 / +0.950R above the gate - and MOMENTUM|STRONG is 20 closed at PF 1.67 / +0.387R. But MOMENTUM|TRENDING above the gate ex-SPX is already 139 closed at 46.8% / PF 2.23 / +0.689R, so the gap the upsizing would exploit is roughly 0.26R measured on 18 trades. Upsizing on 18-20 trade samples raises variance and drawdown for an edge difference that is inside the noise, which is a negative trade on a per-unit-of-risk basis. MOMENTUM|STRONG is additionally not an independent signal: STRONG requires conf>=95 (minimum observed conf among STRONG trades is 95), so it is a confidence tier wearing a different name.
actions.measurableWhy: The replay can re-measure the underlying cells as more bars accumulate, but it cannot evaluate the sizing decision itself - position sizing is enforced by the MT5 bridge, and the STRONG tier is a confidence threshold the replay does not apply.
actions.agreement: setup-forensics and regime-fit both propose upsizing or regime-weighting toward these cells; both explicitly flag the small sample as the risk. This action accepts their identification of the pocket and rejects the sizing move on their own stated grounds.
actions.risk: If the MOMENTUM|SQUEEZE edge is real, the system forgoes the single highest-expectancy allocation available while it waits. The counter-risk - sizing up on 18 trades and taking a drawdown that the measured 0.26R gap never justified - is the larger one at current sample sizes.

blindSpots: Nothing here is live-validated. The journal holds 11 entries and the learning store 9 win/loss outcomes across 218 sessions, while all 826 trades are replay-synthetic. There is no live track record against which any of these buckets can be checked, so every number in this synthesis - including the SPX finding - is a property of the replay, not of the account.

The replay cannot model the MT5 bridge's caps. maxConcurrentPositions is 3 and maxTradesPerDay is 10, so the live system takes a subset of signals selected by arrival order and slot availability. Per-bucket expectancies therefore do not transfer: a bucket that looks profitable in the replay may rarely win a slot live, and a losing bucket that fires early in the session may crowd out a better one. This selection effect is invisible to every analysis in this pack and could be larger than several of the ranked actions.

The replay does not exercise generateSignalMTF. The cohort labels (H4_ONLY, DAILY+H4_AGREE, DAILY_ONLY_H4_NEUTRAL, DAILY+H4_CONFLICT) are reconstructed from single-timeframe outputs, so all cohort-based conclusions - including the rank-6 action and the finding that the conflict cohort is entirely sub-threshold - rest on labels the live combiner may assign differently.

Costs are a single flat 0.05R per trade with no per-asset differentiation, no spread modelling, no slippage and no financing. Since the central conclusion is a cross-asset comparison, and SPX, BTC and Gold have materially different spread and session characteristics, the SPX gap is measured under a cost model that assumes they are identical.

Sizing is a fixed 0.02 lot with riskPercent absent from active settings, so R is not a constant money unit across instruments. Whether SPX's -51.64R is larger or smaller in dollars than Gold's +69.42R cannot be determined from these facts.

169 trades (20.5%) are EXPIRED and are excluded from every statistic. How they would have resolved is a free parameter that no bucket accounts for. The exclusion is not uniform - SPX is 48% expired against BTC's 12.6% and Gold's 18.9% - so the closed-only samples are differently biased per asset, and if expiries are systematically small losers the whole book is worse than measured.

Everything is in-sample on one 2022-2026 window with no walk-forward split, no out-of-sample holdout and no per-year stability check. Buckets like MOMENTUM|SQUEEZE (43 closed) and SQUEEZE_BREAKOUT|RANGING (20 closed) are being used to justify gates without any evidence that they hold across sub-periods.

There is no drawdown, no equity curve, no trade sequencing and no correlation structure between concurrent positions. 'Profitability per unit of risk' can only be approximated by expectancy and profit factor here; the pack contains nothing about the risk that actually ends accounts.

The regime, trend and strength labels are the engine's own outputs, not independent market descriptions. Findings framed as 'setup X does not fit regime Y' are equally consistent with the classifier being wrong, and cannot be separated with these facts - which is why moving adxTrendingMin underneath the proposed regime gates is specifically dangerous.

Whether SPX's failure is a level-scaling bug, a symbol or contract-size mapping error, a bad price feed, or genuine unprofitability cannot be determined from this pack. The 48% expiry rate and the 5.5%-vs-49% win rate split make a mechanical defect the leading hypothesis, but confirming it requires comparing generated stop and target distances against realised SPX bar ranges - data the fact pack does not contain.

The live setting drift is unexplained: maxTradesPerDay is 10 against a default of 5, momentumRsiMax 88 against 72, trendFollowRsiMax 84 against 68, last written by an ad-hoc task named jarvis-daily-unblock-btc. Nothing in these facts shows whether those relaxations helped or hurt, because the replay generated the trades under whatever thresholds it used, not necessarily these.

confidenceThreshold is treated throughout this synthesis as the live gate at 70, and the conf>=70 slice is used as a proxy for live flow. If the threshold was raised recently, or if any code path bypasses it, that proxy is wrong and several rankings shift - which is exactly what rank 6 is meant to resolve.
